title: Review json parse unsafe
why: Parsing dynamic JSON can throw on malformed text, and successful parsing alone does not validate the resulting value's shape.
suggestion: Handle malformed input at the appropriate boundary and validate dynamic values before use; keep intentional exception propagation or trusted-producer contracts explicit.
limitations: Direct round trips and variables assigned from JSON.stringify before parsing are excluded, as are recognized lexical try/catch blocks and tooling paths.

Canonical nonproduction paths with stable named describe, it, or test imports from vitest, @jest/globals, node:test, or bun:test and executable module-level registration use a fail-the-test policy, including their fixture helpers. This exempts JSON recovery advice, not localStorage or other security checks.

Named import aliases are supported. Unknown or global runners, modifier-only registrations, missing registrations, shadowed or reassigned bindings, and quoted or commented examples do not establish the exemption. Ordinary production paths remain eligible; harness recognition is source-based rather than a configured-role query.

Private synchronous named module-level parser helpers can recover through direct same-file callers when every reference is a direct call inside a simple completed try/catch without rethrow. The parse must execute at the helper body level. This establishes syntax-error handling, not validation of the parsed value's shape.

Exported, aliased, asynchronous, generator, arrow-containing and dynamically evaluated helpers, unresolved callers, deferred callbacks and classic scripts do not gain the caller proof. Nested or callback-defining try bodies remain conservative. Names such as safe, schema, zod or validate are not evidence of handling or validation.

This is bounded lexical advice, not proof of an unsafe boundary. Arbitrary cross-function validation, native or subprocess producer contracts and schema contracts are not resolved. A type annotation or successful HTTP status does not establish JSON syntax or result shape.
